absent: Numeric values and bit layouts of page roles, command identifiers, VM types, policy mask and firmware error codes.
Internals of firmware post populate, launch update, finish, decommission, reverse map transitions and reclaim helpers.
Full hardware setup tail including teardown and CPU init helpers not present in the routed range.
Memory ordering and sleeping constraints for slots lock versus file invalidation lock versus all CPU locks beyond observed nesting.
Exact userspace structure sizes, field offsets and alignment for command, region and finish descriptors.

findings.text: SNP initial population entry requires an SNP guest with an allocated context, retrieves a parameter block from userspace, enforces nonzero page sized length with no flags and one of five page roles, uses no source for the zero role and otherwise requires a nonzero aligned source, checks the starting slot for private file backing under the slots lock, delegates to the generic per page helper with firmware post processing, and writes back advanced start and remaining length plus source offset so callers can resume.

Generic populate helper accepts a VM, start frame, optional user source, page count, a writeback permission flag, a per page callback and opaque data, requires the slots lock already held, rejects nonpositive counts and unaligned sources, resolves the slot and truncates the request to the slot remainder, then processes pages in order and returns pages completed or the first error when no progress occurred.

Per page iteration aborts with interrupt status when a signal is pending, pins each source page for read or write depending on the writeback flag, invokes a lower level routine for the target frame, releases the pinned page, and stops at the first failure while preserving the count already done.

Single page worker serializes file invalidation for the backing mapping, resolves the file index and locked folio plus host frame, verifies the target frame carries the private memory attribute, runs the supplied post populate callback, marks the folio up to date only on callback success, then releases references and serialization before returning status.

Population path holds the VM slots lock across precondition checks and the whole generic walk, the generic helper asserts that lock is held, and the single page worker additionally holds the file mapping invalidation lock while resolving and validating the folio and invoking the callback.

Documented preconditions for initial SNP pages are a valid private memslot, prior marking of the frame as private through memory attributes, and a reverse map entry not already private, with the slots lock chosen to exclude concurrent slot updates and attribute races during the checks.

Memory encryption ioctl is the central VM operation dispatcher: it rejects use when the feature is globally disabled, treats a null pointer as success without action, copies in a command descriptor, serializes with the VM lock, blocks disallowed commands from mirror VMs and blocks legacy commands for SNP guests, dispatches by command identifier to dedicated handlers, then copies the descriptor back and reports fault if that copy fails.

SNP finish first measures every virtual CPU state area through firmware update, then optionally loads identity block and authentication blobs plus host data and issues finish; success enables later private page faulting and pre faulting because no further launch update calls are expected.

State area update locks all virtual CPUs, and for each one synchronizes the saved area, transitions its host page to firmware private state, issues an SNP launch update of state area type, reclaims the page on firmware failure, otherwise marks guest state as protected and enables branch virtualization before unlocking all CPUs.

Finish requires an SNP guest with context and zero flags, identity material is only loaded when its enable is set with optional authentication key enable, verification related disable and host data are always conveyed, and temporary allocations for command and blobs are released on all paths.
Certificate request enablement succeeds only when no virtual CPUs exist yet and the VM is an SNP guest, and then records a persistent enabled flag on the VM encryption state.

Encrypted region registration requires an existing encrypted guest and rejects mirror VMs, allocates tracking, pins the user range long term without write permission, flushes caches for correct encryption bit behavior, records user address and size, and appends the entry to the VM region list under the VM lock.

Encrypted region unregistration rejects mirror VMs, requires an encrypted guest under the VM lock, looks up an entry by exact address and size, performs cache writeback, then unpins pages, removes list linkage and frees tracking.
Region lookup scans the VM region list and matches only when both user address and size equal the request, returning no entry otherwise.

Mirror creation accepts a target VM and a source file descriptor, validates the descriptor refers to a KVM instance, locks both VMs in a defined order, rejects targets that already are guests or have CPUs and sources that are not plain encrypted guests or are themselves mirrors or SNP guests, allocates CPU tracking, then under a global mirror lock takes a reference on the source and links the target into the owner mirror list before copying ownership, active state, identifier, file handle, extended state flag and handle and initializing empty region and mirror lists.

Ioctl and region register and unregister serialize with the VM lock held for the whole operation, mirror creation holds locks on both VMs plus a separate global mirror lock only while linking and referencing, and state area update holds locks on all virtual CPUs for the duration of per CPU firmware transitions.

VM type initialization maps default and software protected types to no special flags, enables private memory only for SNP, protected state for SNP and encrypted state variants, allows pre faulting except when private memory is present, and marks encrypted variants as needing initialization while warning on unknown types.

VM destruction always releases CPU tracking, returns early for non guests after warning if mirrors remain, detaches mirror VMs from their owner list and drops the owner reference without touching identifiers, otherwise drains all registered regions with scheduling opportunity, cleans SNP request state and decommissions SNP context or unbinds legacy identifiers, then frees the identifier allocation.

Hardware setup proceeds through global enable plus paging and single step requirements, CPU capability checks, platform driver readiness when built in, retrieval of encryption bit position and identifier bounds, allocation of identifier bitmaps and cgroup capacities, optional encrypted state gating on caching and CPU features and identifier availability, platform probe and SNP initialization verification, then construction of a supported VM type mask.

Encrypted state support additionally requires caching enabled, CPU support for the feature and branch virtualization, and at least one identifier below the legacy minimum; joint identifier space may be partitioned so SNP owns the low subrange and encrypted state owns the remainder, possibly leaving encrypted state with no identifiers.
CPU capability advertisement exposes each encrypted VM capability only when its corresponding global enablement is active.

SNP platform initialized probe allocates a zeroed firmware page, queries platform status through firmware, treats nonzero reported state as initialized, logs firmware failures, and always releases the page.

Population can complete partially: the caller receives updated start and length reflecting pages already processed, firmware status is saved into the command error field while the call returns an IO failure, user copy failures yield fault status, invalid parameters yield invalid status, and signals yield interrupt status with prior pages retained.

Destruction leaks the identifier when SNP decommission fails, warns when mirrors still reference a dying owner, and unpins leftover regions only after userspace termination without explicit unregister, while registration must flush caches before releasing the VM lock because another task could free the region after unlock.

Observed command descriptor usage carries a numeric command identifier, a userspace data pointer, a firmware error field and a firmware file descriptor; population parameters carry start frame, length, page role, flags and source address; finish parameters carry flags, identity enable and addresses, authentication key enable, verification disable, and fixed size host data.

Observed region tracking holds pinned pages with a page count plus user address, size and list linkage; VM encryption state usage includes active and extended active flags, need initialization flag, identifier, firmware handle and descriptor, context owner pointer, certificate enable, context pointer, region list and mirror list linkage.

SNP populate page roles distinguish normal, zero, unmeasured, secrets and CPUID kinds; zero means no source copy, CPUID enables source writeback during pinning, and requests require nonzero aligned length with zero flags.

Legacy encryption commands cover guest initialization variants, launch start and data update and state update and measurement and finish, guest status, two debug crypt directions, secret injection and attestation report retrieval.

Migration and SNP commands cover send start and data update and finish and cancel, receive start and data update and finish, plus SNP launch start and update and finish and certificate request enablement; SNP guests reject identifiers below SNP launch start.
VM type space distinguishes default, software protected, encrypted, encrypted state and SNP kinds, and CPU features distinguish base encryption, encrypted state and SNP capabilities.
